audit_scope.description: This batch covers EL topics: Shanghai state transitions, Prague transaction validation exceptions, EIP-6780 SELFDESTRUCT changes, EIP-7918 blob reserve pricing, EIP-4938 wire protocol eth/67, and EIP-1474 JSON-RPC specification. CL topics: Altair sync committee and attestation processing, Beacon API security boundaries, EIP-8025 execution proof lifecycle, and Bellatrix merge transition and fork choice.

out_of_scope: Execution Layer internals when viewed from CL perspective

misclassified_entities.reason: Sync committee members are validators within the CL system, selected via RANDAO. They are internal protocol participants, not external entities. Their signatures are validated as part of the consensus protocol.
Attesting validators are core CL participants. Their attestations are processed as part of the consensus mechanism. They are internal to the system boundary, not external entities.

The beacon chain network is the CL system itself. When provers receive beacon blocks, the data source is the consensus protocol, not an external entity. The P2P gossip channel through which blocks arrive is the relevant trust boundary, not 'the beacon network' as an entity.

trusted_external_entities.name: User via JSON-RPC (EIP-1474)
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: JSON-RPC API (eth_sendRawTransaction, eth_call, eth_estimateGas, all EIP-1474 methods)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Users submit transactions and queries via unauthenticated JSON-RPC. All input requires full validation: JSON parsing, RPC structure, method lookup, parameter format (Quantity/Data hex encoding), transaction signature verification. Covers EXT-USER from Shanghai, EXT-TX-SUBMITTER from Prague exceptions, EXT-TX-SUBMITTER and EXT-RPC-CLIENT from EIP-1474, and EXT-TX-SENDER from EIP-6780.

trusted_external_entities.name: P2P Peer Node via devp2p/eth/67
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: P2P Wire Protocol (eth/67 message types, snap protocol)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Peer nodes send wire protocol messages including blocks, transactions, and state sync data. eth/67 removes GetNodeData/NodeData (0x0d/0x0e); deprecated messages must be rejected. All block data requires full header validation. Covers EXT-PEER from Shanghai and EIP-7918, EXT-PEER-NODE from EIP-4938, and EXT-SNAP-PEER for snap protocol.

trusted_external_entities.name: API Client via Beacon REST API
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Beacon Node REST API (HTTP endpoints per OpenAPI 3 spec)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: The Beacon API is explicitly warned against public internet exposure. No built-in authentication; security layers (reverse proxy, firewall) are expected at the infrastructure level. Endpoints that trigger heavy computation or return large responses are DoS vectors. Covers EXT-API-CLIENT from Beacon APIs.

trusted_external_entities.name: Proof Generation Engine via Prover API
trusted_external_entities.rationale: The proof engine generates zkEVM execution proofs delivered to the prover endpoint. While typically co-located with the prover, it crosses a trust boundary. Provers MUST validate engine output before signing with BLS. A compromised engine could produce invalid proofs. Covers EXT-PROOF-ENGINE and EXT-PROOF-ENGINE-UNTRUSTED from EIP-8025.

trusted_external_entities.name: P2P Peer via CL Gossip (Execution Proofs)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: SignedExecutionProofs are received from the gossip network. Full validation required: non-empty proof data, proof engine verification, duplicate detection, BLS signature verification against whitelisted prover keys, domain separation check. Covers EXT-GOSSIP-NETWORK from EIP-8025.

trusted_external_entities.name: Execution Engine via Engine API (Bellatrix)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Authenticated via JWT. The EL processes fork choice updates and builds payloads. Content must be validated. During merge transition, the CL fetches PoW block data via eth_getBlockByHash. Covers EXT-EXECUTION-ENGINE and EXT-EXECUTION-CLIENT-RPC from Bellatrix fork choice.

trusted_external_entities.name: PoW Execution Chain via JSON-RPC
trusted_external_entities.rationale: During the merge transition, the CL fetches terminal PoW block data to validate TERMINAL_TOTAL_DIFFICULTY conditions. The PoW chain data is accessed via the local execution client's JSON-RPC, which is JWT-authenticated. However, the PoW data content (total difficulty, parent total difficulty) must be independently validated against consensus rules. Covers EXT-POW-CHAIN from Bellatrix.

trusted_external_entities.name: Block Producer (Blob Fee Calculation)
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Block header (excess_blob_gas field with EIP-7918 reserve price logic)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Block producers compute excess_blob_gas using the modified reserve price formula. Validators must independently recalculate and verify the header value matches. Incorrect reserve price calculations or manipulated base_fee could distort blob pricing. Covers EXT-BLOCK-PRODUCER from EIP-7918.

boundary_edges.security_assumption: Full validation pipeline: JSON parse, RPC structure check, method lookup, parameter validation (0x-prefix, Quantity/Data encoding), hex decode, RLP decode, ECDSA signature verification, nonce/balance checks, fee structure validation (maxFee >= baseFee, priority <= maxFee), blob-specific checks (EIP-4844), init code size limits, authorization list validation (EIP-7702).

Message type validation required: reject deprecated GetNodeData (0x0d) and NodeData (0x0e). Valid messages require full content validation (block headers, transactions). Snap protocol (GetByteCodes, GetTrieNodes) messages require separate validation.
Full block header validation, transaction validation including SELFDESTRUCT behavior (EIP-6780: same-TX creation check), excess_blob_gas verification with EIP-7918 reserve price conditional logic.

No built-in authentication. Security depends entirely on infrastructure-level protections (reverse proxy, firewall). Heavy endpoints (state queries, validator duties) are DoS vectors. Rate limiting recommended. Must not be exposed to public internet without security layers.

Proof engine output crosses a trust boundary. Prover must validate proof content before signing with BLS. Domain separation via DOMAIN_EXECUTION_PROOF prevents cross-domain replay. Invalid proofs from a compromised engine could deceive stateless validators if signed by a whitelisted prover.

Full validation pipeline: non-empty proof data check, proof engine cryptographic verification, duplicate detection by request root + proof type, BLS signature verification against whitelisted prover public key with DOMAIN_EXECUTION_PROOF.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: Engine API (forkchoiceUpdated with head_block_hash, safe_block_hash, finalized_block_hash)
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Engine API is JWT-authenticated. Fork choice updates must be processed atomically. Finalized payloads must be irreversibly persisted. Re-org protection via should_override_forkchoice_update requires all 8 conditions to be simultaneously true.

Terminal PoW block must satisfy: total_difficulty >= TERMINAL_TOTAL_DIFFICULTY AND parent_total_difficulty < TERMINAL_TOTAL_DIFFICULTY. Or if TERMINAL_BLOCK_HASH is set, exact hash match required at correct epoch. Unavailable PoW data must trigger graceful degradation (deferred processing), not block rejection.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: Block header excess_blob_gas field (EIP-7918 reserve price)
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Validators must independently recalculate excess_blob_gas using the modified formula with reserve price conditional logic. Header value must match recalculated value exactly. Both reserve mode (BLOB_BASE_COST * base_fee > GAS_PER_BLOB * blob_base_fee) and normal mode formulas must be correctly implemented.
